blocks.text: At every row, both the old and new object IDs, versions, actor, time, policy, and correlation ID are recorded. The interface offers forward/backward navigation along the chain without granting access outside the user's authorized scope.
G01 — Acceptance. Applicable intake/evidence, conflicts, independence, capacity, and conditions reviewed; partner decision recorded.
G02 — Activation. Current acceptance, signed terms, entity/period/mode, authorized contacts, team, and required commercial conditions verified.
G03 — Planning. Applicable scope, strategy, materiality, timetable, work programs, and EQR/specialist decisions approved.
G04 — Financial intake. Source validity, debit/credit totals, period/entity, mapping, duplicates, and opening/comparative bridges reviewed.
G05 — Production complete. Reconciliations and procedures completed; required queries resolved; AJEs and unadjusted differences have reviewed treatment; adjusted TB approved.
G06 — Senior clearance. Evidence, calculations, references, and conclusions reviewed; blocking notes cleared by eligible checkers.
G07 — Manager completion. Significant judgments, consistency, disclosure, scope completion, and summary memorandum approved.
G08 — Management approval. Authorized management approves its statements/adjustments and supplies required representations; exact versions recorded.
G09 — Professional release. Partner approves report/conclusion; required EQR and consultations complete; no stale approvals or outstanding blocking matters.
G10 — Delivery/filing. Released manifest matches dispatched content; recipient authority and submission evidence verified; failures remain tracked.
G11 — Archive. Administrative assembly, retention classification, legal holds, manifest, restricted access, and next-year trigger completed.
G12 — Reopen/offboard. Authorized reason and scope; records preserved; affected approvals rerun; handover/access/retention actions verified.

No gate shall be represented only by a free-text comment or editable “approved” checkbox. Approval decisions are append-only events with version binding. A rejected decision returns a reason and exact required next actions.

AUT-01. Use native Perfex assignment, task, project, contract, proposal, and scheduled-notification capabilities where they satisfy requirements. Implement professional gates and conditional workflows in the STE extension. Hooks are integration points, not proof of a built-in universal workflow engine. [S6]

AUT-02. Publish events including LeadCaptured, EvaluationSubmitted, AcceptanceApproved, TermsExecuted, ClientActivated, EngagementCreated, ContinuanceDue, DocumentAccepted, ImportValidated, TBApproved, JournalApproved, JournalPosted, WorkpaperSubmitted, ReviewPointRaised, ReviewPointCleared, PackageChanged, ManagerApproved, ManagementApproved, PartnerAuthorized, EQRCompleted, ReportIssued, FilingAccepted, EngagementArchived, and AccessRevoked.

AUT-03. Event handlers are idempotent and scope-aware. Conditions are evaluated from persisted approved records, not from the event name alone. Jobs use bounded retries, error classification, a failed-job queue, an operations owner, and manual replay. Replay shall not bypass a gate.

AUT-04. Recommended operational defaults: inquiry response within one working day; acknowledgement immediately after accepted submission; PBC reminder seven days before and on due date; overdue escalation after three working days; review reminders one working day before due; annual validation 90 days before year-end. These are configurable service targets, not statutory deadlines. Staff absence, holidays, and escalation delegates are applied explicitly.

AUT-05. Notification templates identify record reference, requested action, owner, and deadline, with an authenticated link. They do not include identity documents, complete financial statements, restricted assessments, or bearer access tokens in notification text. Delivery channels, consent and opt-out rules, retries, and message history are recorded.

AUT-06. Project/task templates shall define prerequisites, M/C/O applicability, input checklist, output artifact, role, estimated effort, relative dates, review gate, and recurrence. Completing a task cannot post journals, approve audit opinions, or issue reports unless a separately authorized command passes its own gate.

sections.title: 17. Service-specific workflows retained from the codebase

blocks.text: The following twelve catalogue entries preserve the codebase's intended service coverage. Their task definitions are configurable templates; the target requirements extend them with explicit inputs, review, and deliverables. Not every service uses a TB or financial-statement audit. All services use the common acceptance, terms, access, versioning, review, release, and retention controls. [S2]
17.1 External audit

M inputs: approved audit terms, entity/period, reporting framework, management responsibility, TB/GL, statements, and evidence relevant to scoped assertions. C inputs: inventory attendance, confirmations, group components, specialists, and EQR. O inputs: agreed management presentation.

M processing: strategy and materiality → inventory/cash/banks/receivables/payables/revenue/expenses/assets/payroll/investments/related-party procedures as applicable → fraud considerations and subsequent events → adjustments and completion → statements/report. The optional expansion to a forensic investigation requires separate authority.

Output and approval: supported audit opinion/report and required communications; senior → manager → management approval of accounts → partner and required EQR → authorized issue. Client management cannot select the opinion by acceptance button.
17.2 Internal audit

M inputs: charter/terms, process scope, policies, process owners, control descriptions, relevant populations, and reporting sponsor. C inputs: system access, regulated controls, specialist procedures. O inputs: data analytics and workshops.

M processing: planning → controls/fraud assessment → process and transaction testing → documented observations → factual validation → management actions with owners/dates → independent conclusion → follow-up plan. Cover inventory, banking, receivables, payables, revenue, procurement, assets, payroll, investments, related parties, and policy compliance only where scoped.

Output and approval: internal-audit report, control findings, agreed actions, and follow-up status. Process-owner response does not delete the auditor's finding. Manager and authorized assurance lead approve release; follow-up independently verifies closure evidence.
17.3 Business valuation

M inputs: subject/legal interest, valuation date, purpose, intended users, basis/premise, historical financials, ownership/capital structure, and management assumptions. C inputs: forecasts, asset valuations, debt, discount-rate inputs, market comparables. O inputs: sensitivity cases and site visits.

M processing: preliminary research → framework → financial/operational/market data collection → normalization of financials → ratio analysis → selection and application of valuation methods → sensitivities → reconciliation of approaches → report.

Output and approval: versioned valuation model and report with assumptions, limitations, and supporting sources. Independent model reviewer checks inputs/formulas; specialist/partner approves conclusion; management confirms factual inputs, not the independent valuation outcome.
17.4 Feasibility study

M inputs: proposed venture, objectives, scope, market, capital/operating assumptions, financing plan, timeframe, and decision criteria. C inputs: technical design, environmental/social requirements, permits, and staffing assumptions. O inputs: alternative locations or technology options.

M processing: preliminary research → market, technical, financial, organizational, environmental/social analysis where applicable → scenario and sensitivity analysis → implementation dependencies → recommendation.

Output and approval: study, financial model, assumption register, options and recommendation. Domain specialists review their sections; manager integrates findings; engagement partner approves release. Forecasts are labelled as assumptions-based rather than guaranteed outcomes.
17.5 Forensic audit / investigation

M inputs: written authority, allegation/question, scope, authorized custodians, evidence sources, handling rules, legal liaison where required, and permitted reporting recipients. C inputs: legal hold, interview authority, forensic specialist, regulator reporting requirements. O inputs: advanced analytics.

M processing: plan → collect/preserve evidence → record chain of custody → analyze records → evaluate indicators → authorized interviews → corroborate findings → document limitations and factual conclusions → legal/technical review → restricted report.

Output and approval: evidence register, reproducible analyses, interview records, and authorized report. Access and exports are exceptionally restricted. Professional conclusions distinguish evidence, inference, and unresolved facts. No routine client portal disclosure of protected investigation content.
17.6 Financial forecasting and projections

M inputs: forecast objective/horizon, historical data, model owner, assumptions, business drivers, finance terms, and selected scenarios. C inputs: capex, working capital, tax, FX, funding and covenant assumptions. O inputs: sensitivity and stress cases.
M processing: scope/data plan → historical review → assumptions evaluation → methodology → model inputs/calculations → integrated forecast statements and cash needs → scenario review → findings.

Output and approval: forecast model, assumption register, projected statements/cash requirements, and report. Management owns assumptions; independent reviewer validates calculation and consistency; service partner approves report language. An assurance conclusion is included only under separately authorized assurance terms.
17.7 AML compliance review

M inputs: jurisdiction/profile, regulated activities, policies, customer population, due-diligence records, monitoring procedures, training and records-retention evidence. C inputs: restricted reporting processes, investigation records, and regulatory authorizations. O inputs: system effectiveness analytics.

M processing: plan → policies/controls review → CDD/KYC sampling → monitoring review → reporting-process evaluation → training/recordkeeping assessment → findings/actions → follow-up. The template's suspicious-activity-reporting task means assess or perform only the separately authorized legal role; it is not an automatic report to authorities.

Output and approval: restricted compliance review, findings and action plan. Compliance specialist and engagement lead approve; management receives only legally permitted content. Confidential reporting and anti-tipping-off restrictions are represented in access and communication policy.
17.8 Management consulting

M inputs: business problem, scope, stakeholders, baseline measures, target outcomes, data sources, and decision owner. C inputs: organizational, strategic, operational, financial, market, or change-management data. O inputs: implementation coaching.
M processing: organizational analysis → option/strategy development → operational/financial evaluation → performance measures → recommendations → agreed implementation support → outcome tracking.

Output and approval: assessment, roadmap, action owners, and success measures. Manager/partner review recommendations; client management approves its implementation decisions. Consulting participation shall not silently transfer management responsibility to an audit team.
17.9 Fixed-asset verification and tagging

M inputs: asset register, locations, custodians, ownership evidence, count cut-off, tagging scheme, and reconciliation basis. C inputs: leased assets, disposals, depreciation/valuation policies, and specialist valuations. O inputs: barcode/RFID/mobile capture.

M processing: scope and register acquisition → location/count plan → categorization → physical verification/tagging → reconcile existence and register completeness → investigate differences → validate authorized valuation/depreciation scope → report/update proposals.

Output and approval: verified asset listing, tag register, exception schedule, and report. Register amendments require client authorization and accounting review. A tagging exercise does not, by itself, provide a fair-value opinion.
17.10 Inventory management audit

M inputs: inventory records, sites, count instructions/cut-off, control procedures, valuation policies, and movement history. C inputs: third-party stocks, consignment, work-in-progress, obsolescence, and costing data. O inputs: cycle-count analytics.

M processing: planning → process/control review → count observation/testing → quantity reconciliation → valuation/costing review → turnover/efficiency and loss-prevention assessment → compliance evaluation → recommendations.

Output and approval: count/valuation exceptions, control findings, authorized adjustment proposals, and scoped report. Recounts and unresolved stock movements remain tracked; reviewers approve conclusions before client release.
17.11 ERP implementation and review

M inputs: business requirements, process owners, system landscape, selection criteria, data inventory, access/security needs, migration scope, and acceptance criteria. C inputs: procurement authority, vendor contract, interfaces, segregation-of-duties rules, and cutover permissions. O inputs: phased rollout or independent post-implementation review.
M processing: plan → selection/contracting → design/configuration → migration/integration → testing/UAT → training → authorized go-live → stabilization → independent review where scoped.

Output and approval: requirements/design, configuration and mapping records, test results, migration reconciliation, training/handover, and review report. Client process owners approve business decisions and UAT; technical release authority approves deployment. Implementation work and subsequent assurance require independence assessment and appropriate separation.
17.12 Corporate training on IFRS and IAS

M inputs: audience, needs assessment, learning objectives, selected standards/topics, delivery mode, schedule, materials owner, and assessment approach. C inputs: jurisdiction-specific material, accessibility/language needs, venue, and certification criteria. O inputs: case studies, workshops, follow-up coaching.
M processing: needs assessment → objectives → material preparation/technical review → logistics → instruction → practical exercises → questions → assessment and feedback → completion records.

Output and approval: reviewed materials, attendance, assessment results, and participation/completion certificate where criteria are met. Certificates shall not imply statutory accreditation not granted by an authorized body. Training lead and technical reviewer approve materials; attendance does not trigger an audit opinion workflow.
17.13 Additional accounting practice templates

Recurring bookkeeping: source documents/transactions → posting and bank/control reconciliations → monthly close → management accounts → manager review → client delivery. Each month has an explicit period and close checklist.

Annual accounts/compilation: approved TB and policies → adjustments → statements/notes → management approval → appropriate compilation/non-assurance report where required. No audit assurance is implied.

Review engagement: approved terms and applicable review standard → inquiry/analytical and additional required procedures → reviewed statements and limited-assurance conclusion where applicable. Do not substitute an external-audit checklist without tailoring.

Agreed-upon procedures: named users/purpose, agreed procedures and acceptance → exact procedures performed → factual findings report. The report does not express an audit opinion or assurance conclusion unless separately scoped.

Tax compliance: applicable registrations/rules, TB, tax records → book-to-tax adjustments → computation/return → technical review → client authorization → submission/acceptance → payment instruction and receipt reconciliation. A payment instruction is not bank execution authority.

Payroll administration: authorized employee changes, approved pay rules/time/benefits → gross-to-net calculation → independent review → client payroll approval → authorized export → payment/filing evidence → payroll/GL reconciliation. Payroll confidentiality and access are separately scoped.
18.1 Architectural approach and system boundary

ARC-01. Modular application. The target shall use a modular monolith around the Perfex CRM application, with explicit domain services for practice workflow, client accounting, workpapers, and delivery. The existing PHP/CodeIgniter and MySQL deployment model is the integration baseline. Runtime, framework, database, and module versions shall be selected through a documented supported-version compatibility matrix; the source snapshot version is not a requirement to remain on that version. A separate frontend framework or microservice platform is not required to implement this specification.

ARC-02. Extension boundary. STE functionality shall be packaged through supported modules, hooks, versioned migrations, services, and adapters. Controllers shall handle authentication, authorization, request validation, and response formatting; application services shall enforce transitions; repositories shall enforce scoped persistence. Templates shall render already-authorized view models and shall not implement accounting calculations or approval decisions. Perfex's module and hook mechanisms provide the extension basis. [S6, S12]

ARC-03. Accounting boundary. The practice's own invoices, payroll, expenses, receipts, and financial statements shall belong to the OFFICE ledger. Client accounting shall belong to explicit CLIENT_ENTITY ledgers. A CRM customer reference on an office sales invoice identifies the fee payer; it does not cause that invoice to become an entry in the customer's books. Transactions between the two accounting contexts require separate, explicitly authorized entries and reconciliation references.

ARC-04. Single posting authority. Each accounting entity/book shall have exactly one authoritative posting service and an explicit operating mode. GreenTech capabilities shall be accessed through a verified adapter contract when used. For client books, the deployment shall provide an entity-scoped ledger extension or separately isolated accounting instances that satisfy the same contract. The selected implementation must pass all entity-isolation and accounting tests before activation. Native and custom posting routines shall not both process the same source event.

ARC-05. Engagement versus legal entity. An engagement groups professional work and deliverables. It is not a substitute for a legal-entity ledger. Several engagements may reference one approved entity-period dataset, while one group engagement may reference several entities only through an explicitly configured consolidation scope. An entity's accounts and transactions persist across engagements and periods without copying them into unrelated clients.

18.4 Data and persistence architecture

ARC-06. Transaction store. The relational database shall store client/entity identity, engagement configuration, questionnaire snapshots, structured workpapers, ledger data where managed locally, import batches, approval decisions, document metadata, and outbox records. Every business table shall have its declared scope, key, foreign keys, lifecycle status, concurrency version, and retention classification.

ARC-07. Evidence store. Original and issued document bytes shall be stored privately, outside source control and outside anonymous web access. A document record shall resolve to an opaque storage key, version, content hash, byte length, media type, owner scope, and retention class. A provider's URL is not itself an authorization decision. Expiring download links shall be issued only after a new permission check.

ARC-08. Read models. Dashboards and financial reports may use indexed views, materialized summaries, or caches. Cache keys shall include practice, legal entity, book, period, snapshot version, currency, and applicable permission scope. Financial read models shall be reproducible from the authoritative transaction/snapshot records. Cached reports shall never become a second editable ledger.

ARC-09. Audit events. Record creation, sensitive access, status changes, approvals, downloads, mapping changes, postings, reversals, delivery, reopening, and administrative actions shall emit attributable events. Events shall include an event ID, actor, service identity where applicable, action, object/version, scope, timestamp, correlation ID, and outcome. Protect audit events against ordinary application editing and retain their relationship to source evidence.

ARC-10. Consistency. Operations that must succeed together shall share a database transaction. External calls shall follow committed outbox events, not hold database transactions open. Long-running operations shall expose progress and final results; retries shall not duplicate journals, approval records, client conversions, or delivery packages. A posted journal, its lines, source link, numbering, and posting event shall commit atomically.

Development and automated tests shall use synthetic or approved de-identified data. Production integrations shall be disabled in non-production by default. Email/filing/payment integrations in tests shall use sandbox recipients and endpoints.

ARC-12. Scaling. Web requests shall not wait for large imports, document generation, or bulk notifications. Workers shall scale independently where needed. Scheduled jobs shall use a lock/lease so the same schedule occurrence cannot be executed concurrently. Shared sessions, file storage, and cache configuration shall support multiple web instances when that topology is enabled.

ARC-13. Operations. Backups shall cover database records, document versions, encryption-key dependencies, configuration, and recovery instructions. DATA-01. Every mutable domain record shall include an immutable identifier, practice identifier, applicable client/entity/engagement/period identifiers, current status, creation/update actor and timestamp, and concurrency version. The server shall derive authorized scope from identity and persisted relationships. A user-supplied entity or approver ID shall never override this check.

DATA-02. Required fields shall be validated when the relevant transition is requested. Drafts may be incomplete and shall show missing requirements. Conditional fields shall declare their triggering condition and validation rule. Optional fields may remain null and shall not be replaced by fabricated values, zero, or an empty reference record. Dates, monetary amounts, identifiers, and free-text explanations shall have different types and validation rules.

DATA-03. Use decimal arithmetic for money and percentages; preserve source precision and currency. Reporting rounding is separate from ledger precision. Each accounting policy shall declare the precision and rounding convention. Journal validation shall operate on the values actually posted after approved quantization, not on displayed rounded totals.

blocks.text: 19.3 Cardinalities and integrity rules

DATA-04. One client relationship may have many legal entities and contacts. One legal entity may have many periods and engagements. An engagement shall identify one primary entity and may include named component entities through an explicit membership table. A contact's access to one entity shall not imply access to siblings. An entity-period snapshot may be referenced by several engagements without transferring ownership.

DATA-05. Use scoped uniqueness for entity account codes, journal numbers, import source keys, and schedule occurrences. Unique keys shall include the practice/entity/book scope where applicable. Journal lines shall reference accounts from the same legal entity and book as the header. All related records shall resolve through valid foreign keys or versioned external identifiers; dangling references shall be rejected or isolated for migration review.

DATA-06. Enforce total debits equals total credits in the posting service transaction, together with row checks for valid amounts and accounts. Ordinary row-level constraints alone are not a substitute for cross-line balance validation. A transaction shall reject negative debit/credit representations unless normalized from an approved source convention before validation. A line shall not contain both a non-zero debit and non-zero credit after normalization.

DATA-07. Financial periods shall not overlap within one entity/book calendar unless explicitly modeled as a separate accounting book. Multiple financial statement presentations may reference the same period. Engagement dates, financial-period dates, tax-period dates, and report issuance timestamps are distinct attributes and must not overwrite one another.

DATA-08. Approval records and issued artifacts shall be append-only to ordinary users. A newer version references the superseded version and preserves the old decision. Changing a material dependency shall mark dependent drafts stale and require recalculation/re-review. Issued versions remain historical records and are replaced only by an authorized reissue procedure.
19.4 Source-to-target compatibility mapping
The source mapping is an integration design and shall be confirmed during implementation against the selected licensed versions. It does not require renaming every Perfex table.

blocks.text: API-03. Responses shall distinguish validation failure, missing authorization, version conflict, duplicate accepted request, pending job, external failure, and successful completion. Error messages shall identify correctable field issues without disclosing another client's record existence. Unauthorized object access may return a non-disclosing not-found response according to security policy. Large result sets shall be paginated and scoped before searching/counting.
20.2 Event and integration contract

API-04. Each event shall contain event ID/type/schema version, source aggregate ID/version, practice/entity/engagement scope where applicable, actor/service identity, occurred-at timestamp, correlation/causation IDs, and non-sensitive payload references. Consumers shall deduplicate by event ID and enforce current authorization/configuration when executing external actions.

API-05. Outbound and inbound integrations shall use approved credentials with least privilege, explicit entity mapping, authenticated transport, timeouts, retry limits, and failure queues. Validate webhook signatures and replay protection. Provider callbacks shall be matched to the originating job and permitted state transition. External acceptance shall be verified from provider evidence rather than inferred from an HTTP request being sent.

API-06. OAuth authorization shall record consenting authority, approved scopes, tenant/account, refresh-token secret reference, permitted entities, and revocation status. Tokens shall be encrypted in a secret store or protected encrypted configuration, not in ordinary client fields. Disconnecting an integration shall stop new jobs and invalidate cached authorization, while retaining past evidence. Delegated user access shall not be confused with application-wide authority.

API-07. A document integration shall maintain logical document ID, provider item/version ID, hash, storage policy and permission mapping. A bank-feed integration shall bind each account to an entity, import overlapping ranges safely, and detect duplicates using provider transaction identity plus reconciliation rules. A filing integration shall retain payload version, client authorization, submission and acceptance receipts, errors, and any amended filing linkage.
20.3 End-to-end command sequence

An authorized user submits a validated lead conversion command. The service verifies current acceptance and signed terms, creates or links the client/legal entity, and commits the mapping and outbox event.

The engagement service creates the project, period links, task templates, document placeholders and ownership records once. The notification worker invites authorized contacts only after successful creation.

A contact uploads a PBC document. The document service stores the original, creates metadata/hash, validates the upload, and links it to the request; an accountant accepts its evidential adequacy separately.

The import worker stages the TB, applies approved mappings, and records every exception. A reviewer approves the batch. The system commits an immutable source snapshot or authorized opening/transaction posting according to the chosen operating mode.

The preparer completes workpapers and proposes adjustments. Reviewer and management decisions are recorded independently. An authorized posting or reporting-adjustment command creates the new financial version.
Reports bind to the adjusted TB, policies, mapping and template versions. Review notes must be resolved by the authorized reviewer. Material changes invalidate downstream draft approvals.

Management approves its responsibilities and statements. The partner completes professional sign-off and the quality reviewer completes their gate where applicable. The release command rechecks all gates against exact versions.

Delivery creates an immutable manifest and sends only the authorized package. Acknowledgement and filing acceptance remain separate states. Closure schedules retention and continuance without copying prior approvals into the next period.

blocks.text: UX-01. Display legal entity, engagement, financial period, operating mode, currency, and draft/issued status on financial and review screens. Required fields shall be visibly distinguished from optional fields, with conditional sections appearing when relevant. Disabled transitions shall explain the missing input/gate rather than simply failing after submission.

UX-02. Autosave may preserve a draft but shall not submit, approve, post, send, or sign it. Destructive actions and issue/reissue commands shall display consequences and require the appropriate authority. Search, breadcrumbs, counts and downloads shall respect the same scope as the underlying record. Accessible keyboard navigation and readable validation messages are mandatory.

UX-03. A staff dashboard shall offer “my preparation,” “my reviews,” “awaiting client,” “awaiting partner,” and “failed/pending jobs” queues. The client dashboard shall show requests, contractual documents, authorized deliverables, commercial invoices, and upcoming actions. Internal materiality, audit procedures, review discussions, and firm economics remain internal unless explicitly released.
21.2 Report catalogue and parameters

REP-01. Financial reports shall include trial balance, journal, general ledger, balance sheet/statement of financial position, profit or loss and applicable comprehensive income, changes in equity, cash flow, comparative reports, account history, AR/AP ageing, reconciliation summaries/details, and approved budget comparisons. Framework-compliant statements shall additionally include the necessary notes and presentation checks; a report printout alone is not treated as a complete financial statement set. [S4, S7, S9]

REP-02. Parameters shall include authorized entity/group, book, period/date range, source/adjusted/issued version, currency, accounting/reporting basis, mapping version and comparison basis. Account/dimension/customer/vendor filters are optional within that entity. A firm-wide management report shall be explicitly named and authorized; missing entity input shall not default a client financial report to all entities.

REP-03. Operational reports shall include lead conversion, acceptance/continuance due, outstanding client documents, engagement progress, overdue review notes, unresolved differences, staffing/time budget, work in progress, billing and collection, filing status, completion and retention due. Measures shall have documented definitions and drill-down to authorized records. “Completed” means the approved stage is complete, not merely that a task was checked.

REP-04. Reproducibility requires source version IDs and generation timestamp on report metadata, consistent totals between export formats, and drill-down from each reported amount to mapped TB lines and supporting journals/adjustments. Issued PDFs shall identify their immutable package/version; editable exports shall be marked as exports, not replacements for signed issued artifacts.
22.1 Authorization, confidentiality, and secure processing

NFR-01. All business access shall be deny-by-default and checked on the server for role, practice, entity, engagement, document classification, and current record state. Perfex staff/contact permissions provide a base; STE domain checks shall enforce the additional entity and professional-workflow restrictions. UI menu visibility is not an access-control boundary. [S14]

NFR-02. Staff authentication shall support enforced multi-factor authentication and approved session policy. Client contacts shall verify their identity and signatory authority where required. Privileged roles shall be periodically reviewed. Disabling an identity, changing an assignment, revoking a contact grant, or ending an engagement shall revoke the corresponding access promptly, including background jobs and download-token issuance.

NFR-03. Validate uploads by approved extension, content type, file size, and processing policy. Preserve original evidence bytes and perform preview/conversion in an isolated worker. User filenames shall not determine executable paths. Do not execute imported spreadsheet macros or embedded programs. Documents, exported reports, signed evidence and temporary processing files shall retain their proper visibility and retention controls.

NFR-04. Secrets shall be managed outside source code and business records. Encryption shall protect network traffic, sensitive stored data and backups according to approved policy. Key rotation shall preserve access to historical encrypted data through controlled versioning, re-encryption, and recovery testing. Replacing an application encryption key shall not be treated as a simple configuration edit without assessing data dependencies.

NFR-05. Application logs shall contain operational identifiers and redacted error details, not passwords, tokens, full financial documents, personal identity documents, or signature bytes. Support access to client data shall be time-bound, authorized and audited. Administrative ability shall not automatically grant business approval authority.

NFR-06. Source control shall contain code, migrations, safe configuration examples, synthetic fixtures and documentation. Client documents, production database contents, credentials, application keys, live configuration, session data and operational logs shall be stored in their authorized operational repositories rather than source control. Build artifacts shall be reproducible from approved source and dependency manifests.

blocks.text: NFR-07. Scheduled tasks shall recover from interruptions, keep progress checkpoints where necessary, and expose failed jobs for authorized retry. A retry shall preserve the original source reference and decision history. Partial imports remain staged; they shall not create a partly accepted TB or partially posted journal.

NFR-08. Backup and restore exercises shall test real restoration of database, documents, identity configuration and encryption dependencies, using protected non-production environments. A backup-success notification alone is insufficient evidence of recoverability. Restore results shall be reviewed and retained.

NFR-09. Imports and reports shall support bounded memory, pagination/streaming where needed, cancellation before commit, and safe timeout handling. Cancellation after a financial commit shall report that the posting succeeded and route any correction through reversal; it shall not imply rollback when none occurred.
22.3 Professional records and maintainability

NFR-10. Retention policies shall be effective-dated by record class, engagement type and jurisdiction. Legal hold overrides scheduled disposal. Final audit-file assembly is a controlled administrative activity, not permission to backdate evidence or alter an issued conclusion. Later additions shall identify who added them, when, why, and who reviewed them.

NFR-11. Maintain a supported dependency inventory, automated build checks, schema migration validation, security/dependency checks, and targeted regression tests. Vendor upgrades shall be tested against the extension contract and representative workflows before promotion. Source provenance and permitted use shall be documented for commercial and open-source components.

NFR-12. Business policy changes shall be versioned and reviewed. Template updates apply to new engagements by default; changing an active engagement requires an impact preview and authorization. Previous issued reports remain bound to the policy/template versions used at issuance.

NFR-13. Financial calculation, import, mapping, and approval logic shall have automated tests independent of the UI. At least one end-to-end test shall exercise each enabled service template's creation, work execution, review, deliverable, and closure path. Specialist integrations may use contract tests and approved sandbox evidence before production activation.
This section specifies delivery requirements for establishing the target platform. It is not a retrospective assessment of the source application.
23.1 Approved software foundation

TR-01. Licensed and verifiable baseline. Obtain and retain authorized Perfex and Accounting module source packages for the selected supported versions. Record product, vendor, version, applicable licence, package checksum, dependency manifest, and approved deployment use. Keep protected read-only baselines for upgrade comparison and release reproducibility.

TR-02. Functional reconciliation. Prepare a three-way implementation map covering vendor CRM behavior, vendor accounting behavior, and required STE behavior. Record which workflows will be retained through supported configuration, implemented as STE extensions, or served through an accounting/document integration. Preserve business intent and required outputs without requiring direct edits to vendor core files.
23.2 Configuration and information handling

TR-03. Operational separation. Establish safe configuration templates, environment-specific secret management, least-privilege service identities, private document storage, and synthetic development/test datasets. Authorized operational credentials shall be rotated under a controlled plan. Encryption-key changes shall include dependency mapping and recoverability verification as required by NFR-04. Any repository-history changes or irreversible operational changes require explicit owner authorization and a recovery plan.

TR-04. Reproducible schema. Implement every target table, column, index, constraint, seed reference and version change through reviewed migrations. A clean deployment plus migrations shall create the expected schema without manual database editing. Forward upgrades, repeat execution protection, backup prerequisites and supported rollback/recovery procedures shall be documented and tested.
23.3 Financial and professional workflow implementation

TR-05. Entity-scoped accounting. Implement entity/book ownership on all financial records and queries. Confirm transaction sources, account ownership, opening balances, fiscal periods, mapping, reporting basis, and firm-versus-client distinctions before importing financial data. Enforce scope through services, joins, report queries, document access, background workers and caches.

TR-06. Review and immutable evidence. Implement preparer/checker separation, review-note resolution, manager approval, management authorization, partner sign-off, conditional quality review, issue authorization and controlled reopening as separate decisions. Bind each to an exact object version and retain the evidence and audit trail.

TR-07. STE audit domain. Implement strategy memorandum, materiality, summary memorandum, audit opinion and announcement-letter requirements as typed professional documents with versioned templates, ownership, evidence links, review state and controlled issuance. Retain the project-centric user experience while using explicit engagement/entity/period relationships.
23.4 Data transition and cutover

TR-08. Migration package. The migration plan shall inventory authorized clients, contacts, entities, engagements, periods, accounting records, documents, schedules and approval evidence. Produce a source-to-target mapping registry, transformation rules, row/file counts, financial control totals, exception register and reconciliation report. This is a data-transition exception register, not a code-risk report.

TR-09. Attribution. Assign records to legal entities using documented evidence and authorized mapping decisions. Do not infer ownership solely from a report heading, filename, project label, or proximity in a spreadsheet. Records with unresolved ownership shall remain in restricted staging until resolved; they shall not be assigned arbitrarily to a default client. Preserve original source IDs and documents for traceability.

TR-10. Historical approvals. Preserve historical sign-off evidence as historical evidence. Do not generate new signatures, backdate review approvals, or represent migrated content as re-performed work. Where an original approval cannot be demonstrated, mark the historical status accurately and obtain any new required acceptance/review for current use.

TR-11. Rehearsal and reconciliation. Run at least one complete migration rehearsal with agreed sample and full-scope control totals. Reconcile entity-period TB totals, balances by control account, opening/closing continuity, document hashes/counts, engagement statuses, billing balances, contacts and permissions. Record exclusions and obtain business approval before cutover.

TR-12. Cutover. Approve a cutover window, source freeze or delta-capture method, final backup, validation steps, owner communications, integration switch, and recovery decision points. Production release requires successful migration reconciliation, access tests, professional workflow acceptance and restore readiness. Retain a protected read-only source archive according to approved retention policy.

TR-13. Post-cutover assurance. Reconcile the first live postings and reports to approved source evidence; confirm scheduled jobs, portal access, reminders, filings and billing behavior. Resolve transition exceptions through authorized changes. Do not delete the source archive or dispose of evidence merely because go-live has occurred.

blocks.text: 24.2 Traceability and release acceptance

AC-01. The implementation backlog shall map each delivered function to its requirement ID, relevant lifecycle stage, acceptance tests and business owner. Link source concepts to the target requirement where retained. Changes to requirements shall include impacted screens, data records, migrations, approvals, reports and tests.

AC-02. Release acceptance requires product-owner functional approval, accounting-owner financial reconciliation, partner/quality-owner approval of professional gates, technical operational readiness and data-owner migration acceptance. Development completion or a successful build alone shall not be recorded as business acceptance.

AC-03. Any approved phased delivery shall explicitly identify disabled service modes and unavailable transitions. Production users shall not be shown a completed workflow that depends on an undelivered module. Every enabled end-to-end service must complete its own evidence, review, delivery and closure path.

sections.title: 25. Worked client lifecycle and data transformation example

blocks.text: This example uses fictional records and simplified amounts solely to demonstrate data lineage and approvals. It does not prescribe an accounting treatment for a real client.
25.1 Inquiry through engagement

A prospect requests annual financial statements and an external audit for “Example Trading Entity.” The intake creates lead L-001 with a verified contact route, proposed service, financial-period label and desired completion window. Discovery records transaction volumes, framework, existing accounting system, bank accounts and document readiness.

Acceptance case AC-001 records the ownership documents, predecessor authorization where applicable, competence/capacity, independence assessment and approval conditions. The compliance reviewer completes their review; the engagement partner approves acceptance. Proposal P-001-v2 defines the accepted scope and fee. Signed terms T-001-v1 bind the entity, period, responsibilities and authorized signatory.

Conversion maps L-001 to client C-001, entity E-001 and contact CT-001. It does not create a ledger entry. Engagement ENG-001 links Perfex project PRJ-001, entity E-001, financial period FY-A and the external-audit template. It creates a strategy memorandum draft, service tasks, document requests, review assignments and scoped portal access.
25.2 Source TB and reconciliation

The client supplies its closing TB from an external accounting system. The chosen mode is EXTERNAL_BOOKS, so the upload creates staged batch IMP-001 rather than importing a second set of operational transactions. Required scope, currency, period, account mappings and totals are validated.

25.3 Adjustment to statements

The preparer proposes reporting adjustment AJE-001: debit depreciation expense 500 and credit accumulated depreciation 500, supported by WP-FA-001-v1. The independent reviewer verifies the calculation and support. Management accepts the adjustment. The system records it in the reporting layer; external posting is a separate authorized action.

Adjusted snapshot TB-ADJ-001-v1 combines TB-001-v1 and the accepted reporting adjustment once. Assets net of accumulated depreciation become 22,500, liabilities remain 10,000, and closing equity becomes 12,500, comprising opening equity 10,000 plus profit 2,500. The statement of profit or loss reports revenue 6,000 less operating expenses 3,000 and depreciation 500.

Cash flow cannot be derived reliably from these closing balances alone. The workflow requests opening balances, movements and non-cash classifications before producing its cash-flow statement. The system shall not manufacture cash-flow categories merely to force a reconciliation.

If the client supplies TB-002-v1 already containing the depreciation entry, the accountant reconciles the inclusion and approves a superseding reporting dataset that excludes duplicate application of AJE-001. The previous source, adjustment decision and report versions remain available as history.
25.4 Review, delivery and renewal

Senior review creates note RN-001 against the fixed-asset workpaper. The preparer uploads revised support and submits a response. Only the reviewer clears RN-001. Manager review verifies the full file and financial tie-outs. Management approves the final statements and representations. The lead auditor/partner completes the professional sign-off and any required quality review is completed before issue authorization.

Package PKG-001-v1 contains the final statements, approved report, selected client communications and a manifest of hashes. Internal workpapers are not included automatically. Sending creates a dispatch event; client acknowledgement creates a distinct receipt event. Engagement closure locks professional content and schedules retention and annual continuance. The firm's invoice remains a separately managed office-billing record.

For FY-B, questionnaire ANN-002 starts from confirmed prior facts and asks for changes. A new shareholder, changed revenue band and a new bank account create explicit review items. The partner approves continuance and any revised scope. ENG-002 references ENG-001 as its predecessor and imports only permitted templates/reference data, not prior signatures, review conclusions or finalized current-year figures.

27.1 Glossary

Client: the firm's commercial/professional relationship record. Legal entity: the organization whose books, obligations and statements are being processed. Engagement: a scoped professional assignment for defined services and periods. Book: a distinct accounting basis/ledger within an entity. PBC: information prepared/provided by the client. TB: trial balance. GL: general ledger. AJE: adjusting journal entry. Source snapshot: an immutable accepted representation of external data. Reporting adjustment: an approved reporting-layer change that does not itself post to an external operational ledger. Workpaper: documented objective, evidence, procedures, findings and conclusion. Maker–Checker: separation of preparation from independent review/authorization. EQR: engagement quality review where applicable. Outbox: durable record of committed events awaiting external/background processing. Idempotency: safe repeat execution without duplicate business effects. Issued package: approved immutable deliverable versions and their manifest.
